text: Will AI bring about nuclear disaster?
This is Three Mile Island, home of America's worst nuclear accident. And you see, AI is bringing it back to life.
Microsoft signed a twenty-year deal to restart Unit One.
Uranium pellets in fuel rods split atoms. That makes heat.
Control rods soak up neutrons. Slide them in, it slows.
The pressure vessel keeps the water from boiling.
Hot water loops to the steam generator, and boils a second loop.
Steam spins the turbine, which spins the generator.
Cooling towers dump the leftover heat.
Heat, steam, spin, power. Then, GPUs.
Eight hundred thirty-five megawatts, twenty-four seven, carbon-free.
In twenty twenty-three, data centers used four point four percent of US power. Twenty twenty-eight? Up to twelve.
Google and Amazon plan small modular reactors: Google's first by twenty thirty, Amazon five gigawatts by twenty thirty-nine.
The catch? One point six billion dollars to restart, years to build new ones, and waste with no permanent home.
Of course, AI won't cause a meltdown. But the future of AI might run on a plant from the past.
What should we take apart next?
